items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But the closest people to me, the male friends, were Joe Williams and Cannonball Adderley.

ctx.x: There was something special about your relationship with Joe Williams.

Yes it was. It was like brothers. It was a personal relationship. We loved each other like brothers. He would call me, no matter where he was, every day at 5 o’clock. That’s martini time. That’s when we have a drink. Out of all the males – people – men in my life, Joe Williams was the closest person, I think, in my life, as a male – men friends. I didn’t have many friends. I had a lot of acquaintances and people that I dealt with. Cannonball and Joe Williams were the two people – the two main people that were my…

items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: Through Cannonball I met Nancy, and it just went from one to the other.

ctx.x: And that was it. No contract. No nothing. And the other people I guess came along through the record companies. In those days, especially Capitol Records, almost anybody who was anybody that came through the label that didn’t have management I’d get a call and they’d say — in jazz that is, you know — “do you want to manage this person?” Or they’d recommend me, you know. And that way I remember Dakota Staton was one. She was on Capitol Records and Dave Cavanaugh, who was the A&R man for George Shearing and later…
Somebody take the phone out of your hands—
